summary: SAML assertion with multi-audience drops 'azp' claim in API gateway, blocking feature-flag service RBAC
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of internal requests authenticated via Okta SAML are failing authorization in the feature-flagging service. The API gateway strips the 'azp' (authorized party) JWT claim when the incoming SAML assertion contains multiple Audience entries.

Impact:
- Internal feature-flagging writes and reads fail for service-to-service calls using SAML->JWT exchange.
- On-call dashboards show ~15% of feature-flag API calls returning 403 from ff-service during peak.
- Affects internal rollout automation and an ongoing canary for a payment flow.

Environment:
- prod, us-east region. Okta SAML provider -> auth-proxy (gateway) -> ff-service (feature-flagging).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Obtain a SAML assertion for the service account with multi-valued Audience (okta app config that includes both org and app audience).
2) Exchange SAML assertion for JWT at the auth-proxy endpoint documented in Confluence.
3) Call ff-service using the exchanged JWT.
4) Observe 403 from ff-service; token decoded on ff-service shows missing 'azp' claim.

Observed behavior:
- auth-proxy exchanges the assertion and issues a JWT. When the SAML assertion included more than one Audience, the generated JWT lacks 'azp'. The ff-service RBAC policy requires azp to map the caller to a service-role and therefore rejects requests.

Expected behavior:
- JWT should contain azp populated with the client ID of the originating OKTA app/service so RBAC lookup succeeds regardless of SAML Audience count.

Relevant logs / snippets:
- auth-proxy request-id: req-7c3a6b (attached in investigation notes).
- Example SAML assertion 'Audience' values observed: ["https://app.redwood.com/ff","https://sso.okta.com/org-12345"]
- JWT produced in failing case (header+payload): payload shows no 'azp' key.

Initial hypothesis:
- The gateway's SAML->JWT translation code assumes a single Audience and runs an audience-to-azp mapping that short-circuits when multiple audiences are present, resulting in azp not being set. Alternately, a recent Okta config change added a secondary audience (org-level) which is now hit by a subset of service tokens.

Urgency/notes:
- This blocks internal deployments that rely on feature flags; P1 due to impact on multiple internal flows and canary risk.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 09:40 - Riley: Verified spike in 403s for ff-service correlated with times of SAML exchange. Pulled sample assertions from logs (req-7c3a6b, req-7c3a7).
2026-03-13 11:05 - Ethan: Reproduced locally using SAML assertion with two Audience entries; confirmed JWT missing azp produced by auth-proxy container v3.2.1.

2026-03-13 12:20 - Engineering: Reviewed auth-proxy SAML parsing code path. Found audience normalization routine that trims when >1 audience and does not set azp fallback. Added a debug patch to log mapping decisions (deployed to staging).
2026-03-13 15:30 - DevRel: Confirmed Okta org-wide audience was recently added to multiple app configs (PR: okta-configs#178).
2026-03-14 08:50 - SRE: Rolled temporary gateway rule to accept tokens without azp for ff-service only (mitigation). Observed 403s drop to baseline within 10 minutes.
2026-03-14 10:10 - Security: Reviewed mitigation; approved temporary allowlist for ff-service while patch is prepared.

Ethan Kim (2026-03-13 11:15): I can reproduce. auth-proxy v3.2.1 path responsible. Adding debug logs and small unit test for multi-audience assertion.
Nina Alvarez (Security, 2026-03-13 14:00): Please preserve logs for audit. Don't broadly disable azp checks; if mitigation is needed, scope to ff-service only.
SRE Team (2026-03-14 09:05): Implemented scoped gateway rule allowing requests to ff-service when client_id matches service-account-ff. Monitoring results look good.

Ethan Kim (2026-03-14 09:50): Preparing a patch to auth-proxy normalization to prefer 'app' audience when multiple values exist and set azp accordingly. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521
resolution: Mitigation in place: scoped gateway rule allows ff-service to accept tokens missing azp from known service-account while patch is prepared. Patch for auth-proxy audience normalization created (PR referenced). Plan: merge and roll out to prod canary then global. Post-deploy: remove gateway allowlist and validate no regressions. Pending: formal postmortem if fix spans >72 hours.
